newsitem.title: USA: Ill. lays out financing options for new airport.
newsitem.headline: Ill. lays out financing options for new airport.

text.p: Illinois transportation officials Friday outlined financing options for a new airport southwest of Chicago that they said could be built for a total cost of $342 million to $2.7 billion, largely using general airport revenue bonds.

Kirk Brown, Illinois secretary of transportation, laid out four financing options that included total public funding of the facility and what would be the nation's first public-private financing of an airport.

The public financing plan that involve a hub airport at a total cost of $2.7 billion, or a non-hub facility at a cost of $416 million. Under a public-private scenario, the total costs would range from $342 million to $473 million.

Still, all the financing options would rely heavily on the issuance of $254 million to $2.5 billion of GARBs that would be paid off under lease agreements with airlines that have yet to drop their opposition to the airport plan first proposed by Gov. Jim Edgar in 1991.
In January 1995, the heads of 16 airlines publicly opposed the project calling it "an unwise and speculative investment in a public facility."
Dave Fuschus, spokeman for the Air Transport Association, which represents the airlines, reiterated the group's opposition to the airport calling it "bad idea."
Joe Hopkins, spokesman for United Airlines, said that the the airport was not needed, "and if it's not needed, we're simply not willing to pay for it."
United and American Airlines came under fire by Brown who charged they were opposing the airport because of the near monopoly on the air travel business they hold at O'Hare International Airport.

Brown acknowledged that not a single airline has approached the state about using the airport in Peotone. And the Federal Aviation Administration has yet to act on a draft environmental impact statement for the facility, that a FAA spokesman said Friday was still under review.
